stories.headline: Tiny cave crocs are filmed snatching bats for the 1st time
stories.summary: In Gabon's pitch-dark Abanda Caves, remote cameras caught dwarf crocodiles, the world's smallest, ambushing bats. Living in bat guano has tanned their skin orange, and they're genetically set apart from forest crocs.
stories.why: Gabon is working to protect the caves as a reserve, and this footage shows evolution in action.

stories.headline: Antarctica's only 2 flowering plants found 2 ways to cope
stories.summary: Chilean and Spanish scientists warmed Antarctic hairgrass and pearlwort under small open-top chambers for 7 years. One played it safe and saved water; the other boosted its photosynthesis and water flow.
stories.why: Their opposite tactics may explain why both plants have spread across Antarctica in recent decades.

stories.headline: A bear who rode on mom's back as a cub wins Fat Bear Week
stories.summary: Bear 89, 'Backpack', beat Bear 910 in a public online vote to win Fat Bear Week 2026. Badly hurt in one leg as a yearling in 2007, he recovered with his mom's help and grew into a gentle giant.
stories.why: Fat bears are healthy bears: the fat carries them through the long winter.

stories.headline: Webb finds 'failed stars' just twice the mass of Jupiter
stories.summary: In the star nursery IC 348, NASA's Webb found brown dwarfs only twice Jupiter's mass, the lightest known and far smaller than theory predicts. One even has a disk where planets could form.
stories.why: It's one of Webb's largest images yet, and it challenges how we think stars are born.

fun_fact: The lightest brown dwarfs Webb found weigh just 0.19% of the Sun's mass.
